title: Generative AI for Computer Vision - Week 11 Assignment 11
subject: Generative AI for Computer Vision

questions.question: 1. What is the main purpose of the CLIP model?
options: To learn the relationship between images and text
questions.correctAnswer: To learn the relationship between images and text
questions.explanation: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) is designed to learn joint representations bridging images and natural language text from vast web-scale datasets.

questions.question: 2. What are the two main encoders used in CLIP?
questions.explanation: CLIP consists of two separate encoders: an Image Encoder (such as a ViT or ResNet) and a Text Encoder (a Transformer) that project both modalities into a shared embedding space.

questions.question: 3. What type of learning is used in CLIP to match images with their corresponding text?
questions.explanation: CLIP employs contrastive learning using InfoNCE loss to maximize the cosine similarity of true image-text pairs while minimizing similarity for mismatched pairs in a batch.

questions.question: 4. One of CLIP's important capabilities is:
questions.explanation: Because CLIP embeds images and text descriptions into the same space, it can classify images among unseen classes zero-shot simply by matching image embeddings to prompt embeddings (e.g., 'a photo of a [label]').

questions.question: 5. What is the purpose of prompt engineering in CLIP?
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering in CLIP involves formulating effective text query templates (e.g., 'a photo of a {category}') to guide the text encoder and maximize classification accuracy.

questions.question: 6. What type of data is mainly used to train CLIP?
questions.explanation: CLIP is trained on 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet, enabling broad semantic grounding across diverse concepts.

questions.question: 7. What is multimodal fusion?
questions.explanation: Multimodal fusion refers to integrating information from multiple distinct sensory or data modalities (e.g., vision, language, audio) into unified representations.

questions.question: 8. What is a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed to process?
options: Multiple types of information such as text and images
questions.correctAnswer: Multiple types of information such as text and images
questions.explanation: Multimodal Large Language Models (such as LLaVA, GPT-4V, and Gemini) process, reason over, and synthesize multiple input modalities including text, vision, and diagrams.

questions.question: 9. What is the goal of Text-to-Image Generation?
options: Generate an image from a text description
Convert an image into a text file
questions.correctAnswer: Generate an image from a text description
questions.explanation: Text-to-image generation aims to synthesize visually coherent, high-fidelity images that accurately reflect the semantics described in a natural language text prompt.

questions.question: 10. What is a major challenge in multimodal generative models?
options: Reducing the number of image pixels only
Understanding and aligning information from different modalities
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and aligning information from different modalities
questions.explanation: A foundational challenge in multimodal generative modeling is accurately learning cross-modal alignment—binding fine-grained text concepts to spatial visual elements faithfully without hallucinations.
